text.name: function_spsSprayerSilo
text.text: Four separate liquid tanks behind one SPS pipe connection. Walk into the switch box to choose the tank; any liquid fertiliser or herbicide, each tank locks to what it holds until empty. Pipe-only: no drive-under loading.

text.name: function_spsWashoutStation
text.text: A grated washout bay with an 80 mm hose fitting. Connect a sprayer's water hose and set it to unload: the rinse water from a washout goes down the grate and is treated away over time. A sprayer can also draw rinse water back out of it.

text.name: sps_settingsIbcPersistTooltip
text.text: Yes: emptied IBCs stay on the map (return to store or refill them). No: they disappear when emptied (default).

text.name: sps_settingsPhysicalPipesTooltip
text.text: No: original system - lay and connect pipes at the couplings, chains, sprayer and water/milk lanes; the bought pipes are hidden in the shop. Yes: physical pipes only - buy pipes in the shop, carry them with your hands; every original pipe prompt is switched off. The two systems never run together.

text.name: sps_settingsChemMixingTooltip
text.text: Yes: chemicals bought in the shop are concentrate - pour it into the chem bowl (or any sprayer's tank) and add water to the set ratio; one chemical at a time, wash out with water to change. No: fill straight from silo or IBC as standard

text.name: sps_settingsChemRatioTooltip
text.text: Water parts per part of concentrate. Chemicals bought in the shop (IBC, canister, barrel) are concentrate and priced to match; buying stations sell ready mix

text.name: sps_settingsWashoutValveTooltip

text.name: sps_settingsHoseDirtTooltip
text.text: Yes: the physical pipes build dirt while in use and lying about (wash them with rain or the pressure washer). No: the pipes never get dirty; switching to No cleans every pipe once.

text.name: sps_settingsHoseDirtSpeedTooltip
text.text: How fast the physical pipes get dirty: 1x = the pipe's own rate, 0.25x = four times slower, 3x = three times faster.

text.name: sps_settingsSpillTooltip
text.text: Yes: a physical pipe whose free end lies on the ground counts as connected - open the tanker valve and the slurry runs out onto the ground, leaving a puddle (valves need the pipe lying within 1.5 m of the ground). No: the valve stays shut until the pipe is plugged in.

text.name: sps_pipeModeTitle
text.text: Slurry Pipe System - choose your pipe system

text.name: sps_pipeModeQuestion
text.text:
Which pipe system do you want to use in this game?
ORIGINAL: lay and connect pipes at the couplings, chains, sprayers and water/milk lanes as before. PHYSICAL (new): buy pipes in the shop, carry them with your hands; the original lay/connect system is switched off.
The two never run together. You can change this later under Settings > Physical Pipes.

text.name: function_spsCowBarnMedium
text.text: The medium Rudolf Hörmann cow barn with three pipe connections: slurry out, milk out and drinking water in. The water is a real 35,000 l supply here, so the cows must be watered by pipe or trailer.

text.name: function_spsHose
text.text: A physical pipe. Choose it in the shop: slurry 140 mm, water or milk 80 mm, 4 m or 6 m, and for slurry the ends (female/male, female/female or male/male). Pick it up with your hands (left mouse), carry an end to a coupling and press the right mouse button to connect it. Right mouse at a connected end unplugs it into your hands; left mouse on a connected pipe drops it. Slurry pipes take a colour. Fixed after purchase - sell it to change.

text.name: function_spsDockingStation
text.text: A portable docking post. Carry it with your hands (left mouse) and set it down where you need it, plug a pipe into its coupling, then dock a tanker's fill arm into the rubber boot to load through the pipe.

text.name: function_spsBowserPipe
text.text: The 550 Water/Chem Bowser's own pipes (physical pipe mode). Suction pipe: start end on the bowser's water inlet, lay the far end in a river or pond and start the pump to fill the tank. Small water hose: bowser inlet to a sprayer's or tanker's water fitting. Wash hose: bowser spray outlet, the pump pours the tank out where the far end lies. Their start ends fit this bowser only.

text.name: warning_spsBowserEndNotInWater
text.text: Lay the suction pipe's end in the water first

text.name: function_spsCage
text.text: Strainer cage for a pipe end lying in a lake, river or pond. A pipe only draws water with a cage fitted on its free end and the cage under the surface; pushing water out needs none. Small cage: 80 mm water and milk pipes, either end. Large cage: the male end of a slurry pipe. Carry it to the pipe end and join it like another pipe.

text.name: function_spsTowerMixer
